sentences.text: JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.11.2018.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 17.11.2018 at about 3.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on Honda Activa moped No. KA-04-JM-8803 on NH-75 Kunigal- Bangalore highway Opp. S.L.N. Chicken Centre, near Yentaganahalli bridge, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bangalore Rural District, at that time the rider of the said motor cycle has ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the median wall.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained head injury and other grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala, after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient and has spent more than Rs.1,80,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as electrician and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to do his psychical work or lead a normal life as he was doing prior to the said accident and thereby he has suffered permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,50,000/-
with interest.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared, but in spite of sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to file written statement.

Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement by admitting issuance of 'Act policy/ Liability only policy' in favour of first respondent and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 17.11.2019 at about 3.00 a.m. when he was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 as a pillion rider on NH-75, Kunigal- Bangalore highway, opposite SLN Chicken centre, near Yentaganahalli bridge, Kasaba Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, due to the rash and negligent act on the part of rider of the above said vehicle?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, what rate and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
One witness is examined as PW.2 through him got marked Ex.P12 & 13.
Dr. Nagaraj B.N who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, is examined as PW.2, through him got marked documents at Ex.P.14 & 15.

Second respondent examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.
ISSUE NO.1 :
8. That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint and wound certificate, spot mahazar, IMV report and charge sheet,
which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the father of the petitioner.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar was conducted.

It is the main allegation is that, when the petitioner was going as a pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM- 8803, the rider of the said motor cycle driven his bike in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the aluminum stopper wall of the road.
The contents of mahazar marked at Ex.P3 discloses that the rider of he motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 dashed against the said road side wall.

As per the said Ex.P3 mahazar, the IO has found the marks of the Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
3 accident on the said barricade and cement platform which is in the side of the road.
The Ex.P4 is IMV report, wherein the front and left side body of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 has got damaged.
This shows that the rider of he motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 by driving his motor cycle in rash and negligent manner he himself dashed against the side wall of the road.

The contents of mahazar and IMV report establishes the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803.
10.

Ex.P5 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the rider of Honda Activa moped bearing No.
KA-04-JM- 8803 the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of Honda Activa bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner as the petitioner is the pillion rider.
11. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding of Honda Activa moped bearing No. KA- 04-JM-8803.
12.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence riding.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the grounds to deny the case of the petitioner.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-04-JM-8803 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

4 15.

In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying the case of the petitioner, nothing been elicited to disprove the case of petitioner.

16. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 4 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 17.11.2019, but the FIR was lodged on 21.11.2019 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 4 days of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant has clearly narrated in Ex.P- 2 complaint as to why the FIR was lodged belatedly by narrating that soon after the accident the petitioner Veeresh was initially admitted to NIMHANS and thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, as such they could not lodge the FIR immediately; and the said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
The petitioner is of 25 years at the time of accident.
The endeavor of the parents will be getting the treatment to the injured son than thinking about the legal formalities.

17. Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me)
Hence the delay of 4 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.

18. It is interesting to note that no doubt the FIR was lodged belatedly, but in all the medical records, it is clearly mentioned that the history narrated to the doctors by injured at the very first Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
5 instance, as can be seen from Ex.P.2 wound certificate is that injuries were sustained in an RTA on 17.11.2019 and the petitioner was found unconscious on the road as such
, the nature of RTA was not known to the hospital authorities.
Thereafter as per the very same wound certificate, the petitioner was tested by the doctors on 17.11.2019 at about 6.20 a.m. and shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital immediately.
The discharge summary marked at Ex.7 also discloses that on 17.11.2019 itself the petitioner admitted to their hospital.
These documents shows that the petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident on 17.11.2019.
Further as per Ex.P2 first information along with the petitioner one Hemanth also got injuries and found in the accident spot.
The mahazar discloses the marks of the accident in the accident spot.
Thus even though the delay is caused in registering the FIR, the documents reveals that the delay is caused with genuine reasons.

Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioner after the accident.

19. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-5 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the moped bearing No. KA-04-JM- 8803.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW1 and AW2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the chargesheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.

(Emphasis supplied by me)
Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
6 20.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 5 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P5 charge sheet also supports the view of this court,
as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC against the rider of the Honda Activa moped bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803.
21.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 17.11.2019 which is caused by the rider of the Honda Activa Moped bearing No.KA- 04-JM-8803 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
22.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

The petitioner examined the MRO of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital as PW.2, through him got marked authorization letter and case sheet at Ex.P12 & 13.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :
- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 23 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P6 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 15.9.1995, the accident was occurred on 17.11.2019, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 24 years.
In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala and after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P7 & 10 the petitioner sustained left humerus shaft fracture with implant in sity with head injury and he underwent ORIF with plate and screws.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.75,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P8,9 & 11, amounting to Rs.14,005/- + 17,916/- + Rs.7,961/-= Rs.39,882/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.40,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working as electrician and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2019.

Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
7

As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P7 & 10 the petitioner was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital on 17.11.2019 and discharged on 13.12.2019 and again admitted on 3.1.2023 and discharged on 10.1.2023 totally for a period of 35 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total five months period including 35 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,000 X 5 months = Rs.70,000/-
during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre PW.3, through him clinical notes and X- ray which are marked at Ex.P.14 & 15.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained left humerus fracture and he underwent ORIF with plate and screws.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability for left arm at 45% and whole body disability at 15%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was working as electrician The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.

Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 12%
to the whole body.
As on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 24 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,000/- X 12 X 18 X 12% =Rs.3,62,800/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ;
As per Ex.P7 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 35 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P2 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 35 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.35,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 35 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.70,000/- under this head.

Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
8 h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.3 stated that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.40,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 75,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 40,000/-
c.
Towards loss of income Rs. 70,000/- d.

Towards disability Rs. 3,62,800/- e.
Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 60,000 /-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 35,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 70,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 40,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of Act policy / Liability only to the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-04-JM- 8803.
24.
As discussed in issue No.1 the accident is caused by the actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JM-8803.

The respondent No.2 has taken the strong defence that as it has issued only Act Policy wherein there is no liability for the pillion rider of the insured motorcycle and prays to dismiss the case against it.
In this regard, the official of respondent No.2 examined as RW.1 and produced the copy of policy as Ex.R1.
On perusal of the policy marked at Ex.R1 there is no premium is paid for own damage or to the pillion rider.
The Ex.R1 is the basic policy and premium was paid only for the liability of the public/third party.

In this situation,
whether the policy where no premium is paid for own damages or to the pillion rider covers the death or injuries to the pillion rider of the motorcycle has to be looked into.

In this regard the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 relied on the following judgments by contending that the risk of the pillion rider is not covered under the act policy as the pillion rider of the motorcycle cannot be considered as third party.

25. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.174/2018 c/w MFA.6621/2018 in the case of THE NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.LTD., V/s Sri. Sanaulla Khan and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka had exhaustively discussed with regard to the whether the pillion rider was covered under the act only policy in view of the conditions contains the policy and also held as here under:
"27.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.LTD., V/s Sri. Sanaulla Khan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is pertinent to note that the decision in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. C.M. Jaya has not overruled the earlier decision in the case of Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
9 Amrit Lal Sood Vs. Kaushalya Devi Thapar or New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Shanti Bai.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. C.M. Jaya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Amrit Lal Sood Vs. Kaushalya Devi Thapar or New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Shanti Bai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was a case wherein the extent of the liability of the Insurance Company was in question and while answering the same, it was held that the Insurance Company can cover the higher risk by accepting additional premium.

Under these circumstances, it is clear that the deceased was pillion rider and no extra premium was collected for the occupant of the vehicle other than the driver and therefore, the risk of the pillion rider was not at all covered under the policy.
Under these circumstances, it is evident that the Tribunal had erred by holding that the policy mentioned about the seating capacity of 1+1 and that itself would be the coverage of the policy.
Under these circumstances, the finding of the Tribunal that the liability has to be fastened upon respondent No.2- Insurance Company is not sustainable under law.
The principles laid down therein squarely applicable to the case of the hand.

In the instant case on hand also as per the contentions of respondent No.2 it is a act only policy when such being the case the deceased being the pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JM-8803 is not covered under the policy issued by respondent No.2.
26.
In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.24702/2012 between Jayu Rukya Marathi & others V.s Sheshagiri Yanku Marathi "19.

entities.text: Jayu Rukya Marathi & others V.s Sheshagiri Yanku Marathi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having said so, the liability of the Insurance Company has been rightly exenarated by the Tribunal taking note of the fact that the insurance policy that was availed by the owner of the motor cycle was only 'statutory policy' or 'act only policy'.
Under such circumstances, hardly there is a scope for covering the pillion rider."
27. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.8520/2017 between The Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sri. Mokshith N.J. & others dated 28.05.2024 "14.

entities.text: Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sri. Mokshith N.J. & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law being settled that in case of liability of the Insurance Company, there is no legal obligation under Section 147 of the M.V.Act to cover the risk of the pillion rider in a two- wheeler and he cannot be treated as a third party.

In the absence of payment of additional premium,
the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to indemnify the insured and set aside the order of the Tribunal as well as the judgment of High Court and exonerated the Insurance Company from indemnifying the owner."
28.

In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.4151/2013 between The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Mahadevappa & others dated 07.07.2023 it is held as follows:
"15.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Mahadevappa & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Mahadev Pandurang Patil's case (supra), while dealing with third party with reference to passenger of a car, Division Bench of this Court held that the risk of an occupant of a car, inmate of a vehicle or passenger in a private car is to be covered,
additional premium has to be paid.
If no additional premium is paid, the risk is not covered.

In this context, if the insurance policy is read together, the premium has been paid in respect of personal accident cover to the rider- owner and also third Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/
10 party liability.
The policy did not point out any risk coverage to the pillion rider or any payment of additional premium.

As laid down in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd.'s case (supra), the pillion rider of a motor cycle cannot be treated as a third party in order to cover the risk of the deceased unless premium is paid to cover the risk of the pillion rider or MFA.4151 OF 2013 policy must be a package policy.
Ex . R1 is not a package policy, but it is a limited liability policy or it can be called as an Act policy.
Hence, the Tribunal has erred in recording its finding that the insurance policy is a package policy.
In view of the wrong assumption, liability is fastened against the appellant.

When there was no premium paid to cover the risk of the pillion rider, it is not proper to direct the Insurer to indemnify the Insured."
29.

In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2020 ACJ 98 between The Divisional Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Hanumantha & others it is held as follows:
"12.

entities.text: Divisional Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Hanumantha & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, it is crystal clear that when 'Act policy' is issued in respect of private jeep, the risk of the occupants/ inmates / passengers is not covered by the policy,
unless additional premium is collected and that the risk of the third party alone is covered under the said policy.

This policy goes to show that it is issued as 'Liability Only Policy' for Zone B private jeep.
No additional premium is collected to cover the risk of the inmates but an extra loading premium is collected for Rs.700/-.
This does not mean that it was collected to cover the risk of the inmates as held in the above referred decision.

But the record shows the insurer has got examined its Assistant Manager Sri Shireddy Bheemanna S/o Hanmanthraya as RW-2 and he was examined on 25.02.2012 before the Tribunal.
He has deposed in clear terms that the policy issued in the case is "Liability Only Policy" and it does not cover the risk of the occupants of the vehicle.
He has also deposed that vehicle was used for the commercial purpose at the time of accident and as such, insurance company has to be exonerated from the liability.

Therefore, in view of evidence of RW-2 and Exhibit R-2, being the 'Act Policy' or 'Liable Only Policy', the insurer cannot be made liable to pay the compensation to the inmates of the private jeep, since the risk of the inmates is not covered under the Veeresh.V vs Hemanthkumar.K on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94484261/

In the said judgment also the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka (Kalburgi Bench) by interpreting Sec.147 of Indian Evidence Act has held as hereunder :
"31.
Therefore, the ratio laid down in the Meena Variyal's case (supra) is squarely applicable to the present facts, circumstances involved in these cases.

Section 147 of the M.V.Act prescribes,
requirements of policy of insurance and limits of liability, while in the proviso appended thereto carves out an exception to the main provision.
It prescribes compulsorily coverage of risk to third parties and to those who are stated in the said provision.

Therefore, unless the purchase of insurance policy compulsorily at minimal covering the risk of third parties, the owner cannot ply the vehicles on road or on public places and also in private places.
Therefore, the provisions of the M.V.Act are benevolent in nature protecting right and interest of victims arising out of accident particularly who are third parties.

There is compulsion on the owner for purchasing 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy'
but the owner is at option to purchase insurance policy covering more risk apart from third parties.
Therefore, for covering risk for occupant in the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle, then the owner has to pay additional premium.
Therefore, proof of additional premium is a pure question of fact.

Therefore, where compulsorily purchase of insurance policy covering third parties only the insurance policy is 'Act' Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy' but under this 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/ liability only policy' the risk of occupant of the car/jeep or pillion rider is not covered as they are not be categorized as third parties.

Therefore, by this judgment it is held that under the 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/ liability only policy', the risk of occupant of the jeep/car or pillion rider is not covered hence the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation in respect of death or bodily injury occurred to the occupant of the car/jeep or pillion rider.

Therefore, under these circumstances the appeal filed by the Insurance Companies in the cases of putting burden on the Insurance Companies to pay compensation, are hereby allowed as putting burden on the Insurance Companies are erroneous,
thus putting burden on Insurance Companies is set- aside.
Consequently, the appeal filed by the claimants and owners of the vehicle if they are calling in question exonerating the Insurance Companies are hereby dismissed".
Veeresh.

12 31.

In this view of the matter and relying upon the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, insurance Company mainly contended that it is not liable to indemnify the liability of the insured / respondent No.1, as the risk of pillion rider of the insured vehicle is not covered under the 'liability only policy'.
Further the respondent No.1 had not paid any extra premium to cover the risk of the pillion rider of the insured vehicle.
It is relevant to note that the term 'Act Policy / Statutory Policy / Liability only Policy' and 'Comprehensive policy / Package Policy' are not defined under the M.V. Act.
These terminologies evolved out of practice of purchase of insurance policies keeping in view the degree of coverage of risk.
Covering the risk of third party is made mandatory by the Statute.
Therefore the terminology 'Act Policy/ Statutory Policy / Liability only Policy' is being used.

But if the owner intends to cover higher degree risk above the coverage of risk of third parties, so as to include the coverage of risk of occupants of car / jeep or pillion rider on the motor cycle or damages caused to the vehicle, the owner has to pay higher amount of premium covering these risks comprehensively.
Therefore the degree of coverage of higher risk depends upon the payment of extra premium.
Only if extra premium is paid on own volition of the insured, the higher degree of the risk would be covered, not otherwise.
32. As per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1, the petitioner was the pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803.

As evident from the evidence affidavit of RW.1 and Ex.R.1, the Insurance Policy of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 is a 'liability only policy', under which the risk of pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 is not covered.

The Statutory Insurance as mandated in Section 147 of the M.V. Act does not cover the injuries suffered by the pillion rider of motorcycle bearing or the death of the pillion rider of such vehicle caused in the accident as they are not carried for hire or reward.
They cannot be categorized as third parties and as such the insurer cannot be held liable U/s 147of the M.V. Act.
Further in the instant case there is no proof of payment of additional premium covering the risk of other persons apart from the third parties.
In such an eventuality, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company is exonerated from indemnifying the liability of respondent No.1 insured.
As such the petition deserves to be dismissed against the 2 nd respondent who is the insurer of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JM- 8803.

Thus the respondent No.1 being the owner of said motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JM-8803 is liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
